title: The Thale Cress Reference Genome: TAIR10
description: The Thale Cress reference genome (Arabidopsis thaliana, assembly TAIR10) spans approximately 135 Mb across 5 chromosomes, encoding approx 27,400 protein-coding genes (estimate). This record is the assembly-level overview: the anchor for the deterministic scale chromosome -> gene -> protein product -> pathway -> trait used across this database. REFERENCE GENOME ONLY: a public consensus assembly, never any real person's private genetic data. In the Signature framework this locus is read as a deterministic instruction in the organism's living program: address, operation, and output are fixed by the reference assembly, and every Signature reading stays anchored to the public reference fact.
how_it_works: Genome assembly stitches long sequencing reads into chromosome-scale scaffolds, annotates genes by homology and experiment, and publishes the consensus coordinates everyone references. All records in this database hang off these coordinates deterministically. In the Signature framework this locus is read as a deterministic instruction in the organism's living program: address, operation, and output are fixed by the reference assembly, and every Signature reading stays anchored to the public reference fact.
key_points: Assembly TAIR10: the public reference coordinates.
standards: Coordinates follow the named assembly TAIR10

how_it_works: Scaling walks the ladder deterministically: pick a level, apply its rules, land on the next level. The generator ladder ranks are simple -> most competitive -> mix-and-match -> unmade -> top-notch -> future grade -> god mode. In the Signature framework this locus is read as a deterministic instruction in the organism's living program: address, operation, and output are fixed by the reference assembly, and every Signature reading stays anchored to the public reference fact.
key_points: Deterministic: same level, same rules, same result.
Generator bound: stops at 10^15 records or complete-with-reason.
standards: Scaling claims are structural, not empirical, and labeled as such
citations: JAH Databases genome lane design notes
